summary: Streaming reconnect leads to partial transcript: idempotency-mapping race leaves new WS with only trailing tokens
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when a client reconnects a websocket mid-generation, the new socket receives only the trailing segment of the response (typically the last 20-40% of tokens) and no assistant.metadata/finalization flags. Impact: Customer's UI shows incomplete transcript and no closing metadata, causing the client to retry and double-submit prompts. Environment: Dedicated deployment (reserved pool) in us-west, customers using long-response generation (~12k tokens) over websockets with client-side reconnect strategy. Observed behavior: After a short network blip and websocket reconnect, the new connection gets a partial tail of the original stream; the original connection's socket (recently closed) appears to receive the earlier tokens in internal logs but those were not forwarded to the new socket. Expected behavior: New websocket should resume or receive the entire message (either resume stream from the last ack offset or receive full finalization metadata). Logs/Artifacts: customer supplied 3 client logs, two wire captures, and server-side request_ids: req-845b and req-845b-replay. Attached: client_logs_2024-10-04.zip, wirecap_req-845b.pcap
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a websocket client subscribed to streaming chat on dedicated deployment (long prompt that produces ~10k-15k tokens).
2) Begin generation and allow first few hundred tokens to stream to client.
3) Force a short network disconnect (client reconnects within 4-8s with same client-side reconnect token but a fresh websocket connection).
4) Observe that the new websocket receives only the later tokens and no "final" metadata.
5) Reproducible in customer environment 6/10 times under bursty mobile conditions; lab repro requires forced close of transport while runtime idempotency mapping still points at old socket.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: validated customer logs, matched server request_id req-845b. SRE pulled internal streaming router logs and found an idempotency mapping table (X-Idempotency-Key -> active_socket_id) that had a short TTL. Timeline reconstruction: original socket (socket-A) closed cleanly at 12:03:21Z, new socket (socket-B) connected at 12:03:23Z with same idempotency key. Due to a race, the router forwarded the next token batches to socket-A's write buffer (still referenced in the map) while socket-B received only the final KV-cache-driven tail. Router metrics show a race window of ~2s where mapping cleanup lags behind socket close. Hypothesis: when socket-A is closed but mapping not yet recycled, runtime continues to write into socket-A's buffer (which is drained by internal cleanup job but not re-associated to socket-B). This results in missing early tokens on socket-B and missing finalization metadata because the finalizer routine saw the stream as already completed on socket-A. We reproduced in staging by artificially delaying socket close propagation and observed identical partial-tail behavior. Additional observation: dedicated pool autoscaler and a routing edge cache produce slight ordering shifts that increase race probability under burst reconnects. SRE also noted a gap in the idempotency table metrics and missing instrumentation for socket handover events.
comments: Priya Patel (Support) 2024-10-05: Customer reported intermittent but impactful partial transcripts; supplied logs and timeline.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2024-10-05: Reproduced in staging by delaying close propagation. Suspect idempotency mapping race; creating short-lived mitigation.

Markus Vogel (Runtime) 2024-10-06: Confirmed router writes can target stale socket id if cleanup delayed. Preparing PR to atomically rebind idempotency keys on new connections and to add metric counters for handover misses.

Priya Patel (Support) 2024-10-07: Shared temporary customer workaround: randomize reconnect id per reconnect attempt (client sends X-Reconnect-Attempt header) to force new stream instead of handoff. Customer accepted as short-term.
Diego Ramirez (SRE) 2024-10-08: Deployed TTL reduction and handover-metrics to staging; metrics look stable. Preparing canary to prod next window.
resolution: Workaround: Instructed customer to include a short reconnect nonce header (X-Reconnect-Attempt) for mobile clients to avoid relying on server handover until patch deployed. Short-term platform mitigation: reduced idempotency mapping TTL from 10s to 500ms and added an atomic rebind path for new websocket connections. Long-term fix: merged runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7421 which adds atomic rebind semantics for idempotency keys, explicit handover metrics, and a unit test covering the close/rebind race. Rollout plan: canary to 10% traffic in us-west on 2024-10-09, full prod by 2024-10-11 if no regressions. Postmortem/next steps: add a Confluence runbook for websocket handover, add alert on handover-miss-rate > 0.1%.
notes_follow_up: Add telemetry: handover_attempt, handover_success, handover_miss counters
Update SDK guidance: recommend client-side reconnect nonce when using long-form streaming in mobile networks
CS follow-up: check customer UI retry suppression once finalization metadata is restored
